title: Why cheap things are more expensive
description:
The boots theory of socioeconomic unfairness, explained in forty seconds.

New video every day.

scenes.say: Two people buy boots. One spends fifty. One spends ten. Ten years later, the one who spent fifty has spent less.
The cheap boots last one winter. So you buy them again. And again. Ten winters, ten pairs, one hundred pounds.
The good boots last ten years. Fifty pounds, once.
So the person who could afford the better boots paid half as much for dry feet.
This is the quiet unfairness of being short of money. Being poor is expensive, because you are forced to keep buying the version that does not last.
The real price of a thing is not what it costs. It is what it costs per year.
